nodes.characterization_summary: Ni₃Sn₂-NiSnOₓ-m electrodes show broadened, low-intensity Ni₃Sn₂ peaks at 30.4°, 42.9°, 44.1° indexed to (121), (122), (320) planes (JCPDS 65-9650) besides Ni peaks; relative Ni₃Sn₂ peak intensities increase with Sn/Ni ratio.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As for Ni₃Sn₂-NiSnOₓ-m electrodes, besides those indexed to Ni, relatively broadened and low-intensity diffraction peaks at 30.4°, 42.9° and 44.1° are mainly observed (Figure 2a), which were indexed to the (121), (122) and (320) planes of Ni₃Sn₂ (JCPDS No. 65-9650)

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni₃Sn₂-NiSnOₓ-m show Raman peaks at 482, 806, 912, 1057 cm⁻¹ indicating Ni-O (NiO) and Sn-O (SnOₓ) species in bimetallic NiSnOₓ oxide; relative NiSnOₓ peak intensities decrease with increasing Sn/Ni ratio.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As for Ni₃Sn₂-NiSnOₓ-m with internal standard of carbon (Figure 2b), Raman peaks centered at 482, 806, 912 and 1057 cm⁻¹ were observed, which indicate the coexistence of Ni-O species of NiO and Sn-O species of SnOₓ (Figure S8b) in the bimetallic oxide of NiSnOₓ

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM shows rippled and porous nanosheets evolved for Ni₃Sn₂-NiSnOₓ-m catalysts upon Sn introduction compared to aggregated particles of Ni-NiOₓ.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) analysis indicated that Ni-NiOₓ exists in the form of aggregated particles... Upon the introduction of Sn, rippled and porous nanosheets were evolved for the Ni₃Sn₂-NiSnOₓ-m catalysts

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS analysis and mapping demonstrate uniform distribution of Ni, Sn and O throughout Ni₃Sn₂-NiSnOₓ-m catalysts.
nodes.evidence_snippet: To examine the elemental composition and distribution in Ni₃Sn₂-NiSnOₓ-m catalysts, energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) analysis and EDS mapping images were collected, which demonstrated the uniformly distribution of Ni, Sn and O

nodes.characterization_summary: AC-HRTEM shows crystalline Ni₃Sn₂ NPs (lattice fringes 0.205 nm (320), 0.208 nm (311), 0.210 nm (122), 0.226 nm (310), 0.243 nm (031), 0.294 nm (121) facets; interplanar angles 63° and 53°) and amorphous NiSnOₓ with distinct interfaces; Ni₃Sn₂ NP sizes decrease then increase, densities increase with Sn/Ni ratio; Ni₃Sn₂-NiSnOₓ-2 has smallest NPs (avg. 2.1 nm).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The observed lattice fringe spacings of 0.205, 0.208, 0.210, 0.226, 0.243, and 0.294 nm for the Ni₃Sn₂-NiSnOₓ-2 could be assigned to (320), (311), (122), (310), (031) and (121) facets of Ni₃Sn₂, respectively... the angles of the two pairs of planes are 63° and 53°... Ni₃Sn₂-NiSnOₓ-2 exhibits the smallest Ni₃Sn₂ NPs with average diameters of ca. 2.1 nm

nodes.characterization_summary: SAED pattern confirms polycrystalline Ni₃Sn₂ domains with highly diffused halo from amorphous NiSnOₓ.
nodes.evidence_snippet: These results collectively manifest the ploycrystalline domains of Ni₃Sn₂ NPs with different crystal planes, which is further confirmed by the selected-area electron diffraction (SAED) pattern (Figure 2e). A highly diffused halo appeared on the SAED pattern, which is assigned to amorphous NiSnOₓ component

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM and EDS mappings reveal clearly defined Ni₃Sn₂-NiSnOₓ nanocomposites in Ni₃Sn₂-NiSnOₓ-2 catalyst.
nodes.evidence_snippet: High-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopic (HAADF-STEM) image and the EDS mappings (Figure 2f) further revealed the clearly defined Ni₃Sn₂-NiSnOₓ nanocomposites for Ni₃Sn₂-NiSnOₓ-2 catalyst

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni 2p and Sn 3d BEs in Ni₃Sn₂-NiSnOₓ-2 shifted +0.64 eV and -1.07 eV vs Ni-NiOₓ/Sn-SnOₓ indicating strong Ni-Sn interaction; both show Ni⁰/Sn⁰ and Ni²⁺/Sn²⁺/⁴⁺ states; Ni⁰/Sn⁰ ratio ~1.6 matches Ni₃Sn₂ stoichiometry; metallic state contributions vary systematically with Sn/Ni ratio and surface treatments.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the binding energies (BEs) of Ni 2p and Sn 3d of the Ni₃Sn₂-NiSnOₓ-2 catalyst are positively and negatively shifted by ca. 0.64 and 1.07 eV, respectively... the Ni⁰/Sn⁰ ratio of the sample is estimated to be ca. 1.6... the metallic state contributions (Ni⁰ and Sn⁰) for all the as-prepared samples increased with increasing Sn/Ni feeding ratio initially and then decreased
